chunks: And Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorified, made Hajj obligatory upon those with capacity every year.

And this is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorified: 'And to Allah belongs the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it. And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.'
I asked: 'And whoever among us does not perform Hajj has disbelieved?' He said: 'No, but whoever says
The meaning of these narrations is that it is obligatory upon those with capacity every year in the manner of substitution (cumulative).

Because whoever Hajj becomes obligatory upon him in the first year and does not do it, it becomes obligatory upon him in the second year, and likewise if he does not perform Hajj in the second year, it becomes obligatory upon him in the third year, and in this manner every year until he performs it.
And they (peace be upon them) did not mean that it is obligatory upon them every year in the manner of accumulation (i.e., one for each year).

And similar to this is what we say regarding the obligation of the three expiations, that whenever he does not perform one of them, we say that each one of them has the attribute of obligation; so when he performs one of them, the remaining ones cease to be obligatory.
And so is the saying regarding what these narrations contain.

key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْبَدَلِ: In the manner of substitution (cumulative obligation)
key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْجَمْعِ: In the manner of accumulation (multiple distinct obligations)

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj obligatory every year for those who are able, and how are missed years handled?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while Hajj is technically obligatory annually for the capable, it functions via substitution (al-badal) rather than accumulation (al-jam'), meaning a missed year does not create a new, separate debt but rather extends the single obligation until fulfilled. This distinction prevents the burden of multiple Hajjs from becoming excessive, paralleling the Shia legal principle regarding the three expiations (kaffarat) where performing one discharges the obligation for all. The Imam further refines the concept of 'disbelief' (kafara) mentioned in the verse, specifying it refers to denying the obligation itself rather than merely failing to perform it due to delay.
